partners.diseaseBName: congenital disorder of glycosylation, type IIaa
partners.mechanism_chain: BET1 (HGNC:1121) —DISRUPTS→ Golgi apparatus (GO:0005794); STX5 (HGNC:11202) —DISRUPTS→ Golgi apparatus (GO:0005794); Golgi apparatus (GO:0005794) —LEADS_TO→ protein transport (GO:0015907); protein transport (GO:0015907) —LEADS_TO→ protein N-linked glycosylation (GO:0006486); protein transport (GO:0015907) —LEADS_TO→ muscular dystrophy, congenital, with rapid progression (MONDO:0009682); protein N-linked glycosylation (GO:0006486) —LEADS_TO→ congenital disorder of glycosylation, type IIaa (MONDO:0957540). Mutations in BET1 and STX5 disrupt the function of the Golgi apparatus, impairing intra-Golgi protein transport. This general defect in protein transport affects the maturation of muscle proteins leading to congenital muscular dystrophy. Concurrently, the impaired Golgi function disrupts the N-linked glycosylation pathway, manifesting as congenital disorder of glycosylation type IIaa.

falsification.text: If mutations in BET1 or STX5 were found to be exclusively associated with either muscular dystrophy or CDG IIaa, and not implicated in the other, this mechanistic link would be falsified. falsification.gnomad_variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 1%) in the coding regions of BET1 or STX5 in the general population (e.g., gnomAD) that do not segregate with either disease.

partners.mechanism_chain: BET1 (HGNC:1113) —DISRUPTS→ ER to Golgi transport; SAR1B (HGNC:10591) —DISRUPTS→ ER to Golgi transport; ER to Golgi transport —LEADS_TO→ Vesicle trafficking; Vesicle trafficking —LEADS_TO→ Impaired muscle development (HP:0003691); Vesicle trafficking —LEADS_TO→ Impaired lipid absorption (HP:0030049). ### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. congenital disorder of glycosylation, type IIaa  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.431)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-204005, Reactome:R-HSA-6807878)

**Proposed mechanism:** BET1 (HGNC:1121) —DISRUPTS→ Golgi apparatus (GO:0005794); STX5 (HGNC:11202) —DISRUPTS→ Golgi apparatus (GO:0005794); Golgi apparatus (GO:0005794) —LEADS_TO→ protein transport (GO:0015907); protein transport (GO:0015907) —LEADS_TO→ protein N-linked glycosylation (GO:0006486); protein transport (GO:0015907) —LEADS_TO→ muscular dystrophy, congenital, with rapid progression (MONDO:0009682); protein N-linked glycosylation (GO:0006486) —LEADS_TO→ congenital disorder of glycosylation, type IIaa (MONDO:0957540). Mutations in BET1 and STX5 disrupt the function of the Golgi apparatus, impairing intra-Golgi protein transport. This general defect in protein transport affects the maturation of muscle proteins leading to congenital muscular dystrophy. Concurrently, the impaired Golgi function disrupts the N-linked glycosylation pathway, manifesting as congenital disorder of glycosylation type IIaa.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in BET1 or STX5 were found to be exclusively associated with either muscular dystrophy or CDG IIaa, and not implicated in the other, this mechanistic link would be falsified. Furthermore, demonstrating that the Golgi apparatus and protein transport are not functionally impaired in one of the conditions would also refute the hypothesis. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 1%) in the coding regions of BET1 or STX5 in the general population (e.g., gnomAD) that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of BET1 and STX5 in Golgi function and protein transport could lead to therapeutic strategies that target these pathways for both congenital muscular dystrophy and CDG type IIaa, potentially improving protein maturation, transport, and glycosylation.
